anomalies.observed: The MAX3485 B pin (U2 pin 7) sits only on Net-(U2-B), which also joins R5 pin 2 (R5 to +3V3) and R24 pin 1 (R24 to GND). No connector, servo signal or jumper reaches this net. The A pin (U2 pin 6, /NET0024) does reach the servo bus through R7 (0 Ω) to the Net-(J5-Pin_3) servo signal.
anomalies.expected: A bias network on the B line only makes sense if B is tied to the same single-wire servo bus as A. The spec describes the MAX3485 as converting the UART to a shared single-wire TTL servo bus, with pull networks on the A/B lines.

evidence.quote: R6, R7, R8, R15 | 2k, 20k, 2.2k, 2.2k | Bias/pull network on the MAX3485 A/B differential lines and DE/RE enable line.

anomalies.impact: Only the A line reaches the servo bus. The B side is held at a mid-rail bias by the R5/R24 divider and does not drive or receive the servo line. In serial mode the half-duplex bus may not switch correctly, or receive threshold and fail-safe behaviour may be degraded. This is uncertain, because a single-ended use of A with an internal B bias can be a deliberate reference arrangement.

parsed.summary: Most of the netlist matches the spec's power, battery-switch, servo-jumper and RS-485 structure, although reference designators differ from the spec. The one suspicious finding is that the MAX3485 B line is connected only to its bias resistors and never reaches the servo bus, while A does. This is plausibly an open connection but could be an intentional reference arrangement, so confidence is low.
